relations.evidence: The Eventing Function lifecycle operations (deploying, undeploying, pausing, resuming, and deleting operations) and the Eventing rebalance operation **are mutually exclusive**. The Eventing rebalance operation fails when an Eventing Function lifecycle operation is currently in progress. Likewise, when the Eventing rebalance operation is in progress, you cannot perform an Eventing Function lifecycle operation.

relations.evidence: **OnDeploy Timeout**: OnDeploy Timeout defines the maximum duration allowed for an Eventing Function to complete its initialization during deployment or resumption. The OnDeploy entry point must complete execution, from start to end, within the specified timeout period. If the runtime exceeds the specified duration, the function is reverted to its previous state. By default, the timeout is set to 60 seconds.

relations.subject: eventing:timer
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; object is a literal
relations.evidence: **Timer Context Max Size**: Timer Context Max Size limits the size of the context for any Timer created by the Function. Eventing Timers can store and access a context which can be any JSON document, the context is used to store state when the timer is created and retrieve state when the timer fires. By default the size is 1024 bytes, but this can be adjusted on a per Function basis.

notable_absence.finding: Exactly as in the Capella twin, this UI walkthrough never names a Capella project role or an edition badge, and instead assumes the reader has the classic 'Full Admin' or 'Eventing Full Admin' role or points to eventing-rbac.md otherwise. Consistent with the pattern seen across this batch: server/ pages default to the classic on-premise RBAC catalogue, not because the docs decided against Capella-role gating, but because the concept does not exist on this deployment target at all.

cross_component_finding: This page's Settings table (Table 1) is byte-for-byte identical prose to the Capella twin's version (verified directly - the same paragraph describing System Log Level, Application log location, SQL++ Consistency, Workers, Language compatibility, Script Timeout, OnDeploy Timeout and Timer Context Max Size appears unchanged in cloud/eventing/eventing-lifecycle.md), yet the round-8 Capella extraction record never captured a single one of these settings or the OnDeploy() entry point as a concept - the twin's concepts[] array stops at eventing:function-scope/listen-to-location/eventing-storage/deployment-feed-boundary/rebalance-operation and the two classic roles. OnDeploy() is a genuine third Eventing entry point (alongside the already-promoted OnUpdate/OnDelete) that fires once per deployment/resumption for Function initialization rather than per-mutation, and it appears identically on both trees - so this is not a Server-vs-Capella content difference, it is a completeness gap in the prior round's extraction of a page it had equal access to. A later reconciliation pass should consider re-extracting cloud/eventing/eventing-lifecycle.md, or accept this record's eventing:on-deploy-handler/eventing:constant-binding mints as also applicable there, rather than treating the two trees' concept counts for this page as meaningfully different.
